This paper establishes a novel ill-posedness result regarding the dimensionless steady Navier-Stokes equations in critical Besov spaces. Specifically, we demonstrate that for any given initial data within the critical homogeneous Besov space $B^{\frac{3}{p'}_ {p',1} }$ (where $1<p<\infty$), there exists a perturbation of arbitrarily small norm such that the corresponding steady Navier-Stokes equations lack a weak solution. Our methodology relies on constructing a specific class of compactly supported periodic functions and applying the Raikov theorem. Furthermore, our findings extend the previously established ill-posedness results by Fabes, Jones, and Rivi\`ere \cite{FJR1995} and Kozono, Yamazaki, and Yamamoto \cite{KY2001} to the setting of critical Besov spaces. Finally, we illustrate an explicit scenario in which the steady Navier-Stokes equations fail to produce a steady solution. Consequently, this work addresses a question originally posed by Fabes, Jones, and Rivi\`ere \cite{FJR1995} in the context of the steady Navier-Stokes equations. Additionally, our results yield a distinct and significant improvement over the ill-posedness theorems previously achieved by Fabes, Jones, and Rivi\`ere \cite{FJR1995} and Kozono, Yamazaki, and Yamamoto \cite{KY2001}. Finally, the ill-posedness result for the steady Navier-Stokes equations derived in this paper is also distinct from the ill-posedness theorem concerning the Cauchy problem for time-dependent Navier-Stokes equations. This latter result was established by Kozono, Yamazaki, and Yamamoto \cite{KY2001}, Kozono, Planchon, and Smith \cite{KPS2004}, and Kozono, Planchon, Smith, and Yamazaki \cite{KPSY2005} within the framework of critical homogeneous Besov spaces. \textbf{Keywords:} Besov spaces; ill-posedness; steady Navier-Stokes equations. \textbf{AMS Subject Classification:} 35Q30; 35R35; 35R60. \textbf{Mathematics Subject Classification:} 35Q30; 35R

Loidreau's code-based cryptography relies on the security of the syndrome decoding problem within Goppa codes. This approach extends traditional code-based schemes by substitging Goppa codes with Twisted Goppa codes, which offer a smaller public key while maintaining equivalent security levels. However, the algebraic structure inherent in Goppa codes also introduces vulnerabilities exploitable via algebraic attacks. To address this, we propose two modifications to Loidreau's system, utilizing Goppa codes with extended lengths to enhance security against these algebraic methods. The first variant employs a public key size comparable to the original, with only a marginal decrease in speed. The second variant offers a significant reduction in public key size, though it results in a notable slowdown. Experimental evidence supports the efficacy of both proposed variants. Additionally, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of the computational complexities associated with various attacks, including algebraic attacks, differential attacks, and attacks leveraging the rank metric. Finally, we investigated the feasibility of attacks targeting the syndrome matrix in our proposed system and demonstrated that the rank metric is insufficient for protecting the syndrome matrix against such attacks. These findings underscore the necessity of using Goppa codes with extended lengths in lattice-based code constructions to ensure robust security. Our results indicate that the public key public key size is a critical factor in determining the overall system's security. Furthermore, we examined the attack landscape of our proposed system and identified the public key size as a fundamental element influencing both security and performance. These insights have been incorporated into the design of our code-based lattice system. The source code is available at: https://github.com/ehsan-mohammadi/Twisted-Goppa-code. Keywords: Post-Quantum Cryptography, Twisted Goppa Codes, Rank Metric, Lattice-Based Cryptography.

We present Dict-BERT, a BERT variant that enhances standard pre-training by incorporating glossaries. In this approach, glossaries serve as explicit knowledge within the training pipeline, allowing the model to learn the mappings between general terms and their definitions. This method leverages the well-established expertise found in Baidu Baike, the leading Chinese knowledge encyclopedia. By integrating glossaries, we deepen the model's understanding of domain-specific concepts and clarify ambiguous word meanings. Experimental results demonstrate that Dict-BERT surpasses BERT-base on the GLUE benchmark by 1.4 points, achieving 83.16% accuracy. Furthermore, it outperforms BERT on Baidu Baike by a margin of 4.55, indicating superior ability in generating knowledge article content. Additionally, the pre-trained model gains a distinct advantage in disambiguation tasks, as evidenced by a 2.11-point improvement in Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD) scores over BERT. The implementation code is available at https://github.com/Dict-BERT/Dict-BERT. Our models can be accessed at https://github.com/Dict-BERT/Dict-BERT. This study derives the volume of minimal spanning complexes within random 2-complexes, such as random triangulated surfaces. It demonstrates that the minimal spanning 2-complexes of random simplicial complexes converge to a specific random geometric object known as a "continuity diagram." Furthermore, an application of this finding establishes the minimality of the "infinite fan triangulation" for the sphere. The research also examines the characteristics of minimal spanning acycles in the context of higher-dimensional simplicial complexes. Additionally, the paper explores the identification of the minimal free resolution for the ideals associated with these random complexes. Finally, the work investigates the relationship between the Betti numbers of these random complexes and those of their minimal spanning complexes. Finally, the sphere is triangulated into various configurations.

Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) represents a privacy-preserving framework where multiple data holders possessing data from different dimensions collaborate to train a shared machine learning model. However, when these data holders are adversaries, the very mechanisms designed to safeguard privacy can be repurposed as vulnerabilities to launch attacks on both the data and the models. This paper introduces the field of Pragmatic Privacy Assaults on Vertical Federated Education (PPAVVE), which encompasses attacks against every stage of a VFL educational pipeline. This pipeline includes data collection, preprocessing, model construction, continuous learning, and privacy preservation. The objective of PPAVVE is to reveal the inherent weaknesses in VFL pipelines and to inspire research into more robust and resilient VFL educational systems. To achieve this, the paper outlines the definition and scope of PPAVVE, provides a comprehensive taxonomy of its constituent attacks, and offers specific examples for each category. Finally, PPAVVE serves as a foundational resource for advancing research into the security and privacy resilience of VFL educational environments. Additionally, the paper offers guidance for developing strategies to fortify VFL pipelines against the various threats identified. A key contribution is the introduction of a novel privacy preservation technique for VFL pipelines, which is demonstrated to effectively counter PPAVVE. The study concludes by identifying open challenges and proposing directions for future research. Finally, to facilitate empirical evaluation, the authors have made their VFL pipeline, along with the proposed privacy preservation method and associated experiments, publicly available. This includes providing access to the complete code, datasets, and results for reproducibility purposes. The code repository can be accessed at: https://github.com/ChenYi2020/VFL_Pipeline. Furthermore, a research paper detailing this work is available at: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.10001. In supervised machine learning, mislabeling inevitably occurs, introducing label noise that degrades model performance. While various label noise correction methods exist, they often suffer from high computational costs or lack of parallelism. This paper introduces a novel algorithm designed to mitigate label noise by partitioning the training dataset into multiple subsets and identifying the most reliable ones. The proposed approach, Bag Sampling and Group-based Loss (BSGL), is validated through experiments on two publicly available datasets. The results demonstrate that BSGL not only enhances model accuracy but also executes more rapidly than existing state-of-the-art solutions. Furthermore, the method exhibits robustness against diverse noise ratios and remains effective across different classifier architectures. Finally, comprehensive analyses are provided to illustrate the algorithm's underlying mechanisms. Code is accessible at https://github.com/ChenYi1998/BSGL. Keywords: Label noise, data retrieval, ranking, bag sampling, group-based loss.

Label scarcity remains a critical hurdle for graph classification tasks. While data augmentation techniques have proven effective in addressing this label limitation, their application is often constrained by the specific characteristics of individual datasets. This paper introduces a novel and generalizable data augmentation framework for graph classification that leverages subgraph isomorphism. Our approach employs a recursive algorithm to generate pseudo-labels for subgraphs, utilizing graph neural networks to aggregate these labels at the node level. These node-level labels subsequently guide the creation of augmented graphs, which are optimized to enhance the predictive performance of the target model. Experimental results demonstrate that our method surpasses current state-of-the-art approaches across a diverse range of graph datasets. The code is accessible at https://github.com/ChenchenLi1992/ICML22-GDA. Furthermore, the paper is available in English or Chinese. Keywords: data augmentation, label scarcity, graph isomorphism, graph neural networks.

The AWAKE experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider aims to investigate self-modulation and plasma wakefield acceleration by propagating a proton beam through a plasma channel. This study examines betatron radiation emitted by the plasma electrons during the self-modulation phase. We present a detailed radiation transport simulation of the proton- plasma interaction, utilizing the plasma emission spectrum from self-modulating protons to calculate the resulting radiation transport spectrum. Furthermore, this radiation is expected to generate electron-positron pairs, which we analyze in detail. We have also computed the average number of generated pairs and identified the primary mechanisms driving their production. Additionally, we discuss the impact of these pairs on the plasma electron beam and the potential for detecting the radiation. These findings are intended to guide experimental efforts to observe betatron radiation and pair generation in future AWAKE Run 2 experiments.

This study introduces a series of algorithms for distributed decision tree learning that adhere to differential privacy principles. Leveraging the local randomness of these methods, we establish a privacy guarantee by quantifying the maximum sensitivity of decision trees relative to local dataset perturbations, specifically using the Local L1 norm. We propose a privacy mechanism grounded in the randomized response technique to ensure differential privacy. By integrating advanced tree sensitivity analysis with a novel noise addition strategy, we construct differentially private decision tree learning algorithms. We demonstrate that these proposed algorithms can be decomposed into a collection of expandable and precise probabilistic algorithms. Furthermore, we empirically validate the practicality of our approach and benchmark it against the heuristic algorithm proposed by Li et al. on the California Housing dataset, showing that our methods achieve comparable accuracy. Finally, we illustrate the distinct advantages of these algorithms through various numerical experiments. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/ChenchenLi1998/DPTree.

By applying successive regularizations, the problem is transformed into a family of rényi entropy maximization tasks subject to moment constraints. This reformulation enables the application of Bregman proximal gradient methods, which rely on specific properties of both the objective function and the constraints. These properties are analyzed across various choices of the Rényi parameter $\alpha$, covering both information-theoretic and generalized contexts. Furthermore, the analysis examines the relationship between the sequences of rényi entropy maximizers and the original rényi distance minimizers in the limit as $\alpha$ approaches zero. Finally, a comprehensive numerical study is conducted to evaluate the performance of these algorithms on both synthetic and real-world datasets. The results demonstrate that Bregman proximal gradient methods are effective for rényi divergence minimization, particularly when $\alpha$ is small. Additionally, regularized rényi entropy maximization yields satisfactory solutions for approximate maximum likelihood estimation and clustering. The proposed algorithms are effective for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian data, offering a significant advantage over traditional maximum likelihood estimators in high-dimensional settings. Finally, the paper explores the connection between rényi entropy and the information bottleneck framework. Regularized rényi entropy maximization serves as a key component in this framework, specifically for learning generative models and conducting clustering. The paper concludes by detailing the implementation of this approach for clustering. Implementing the information bottleneck requires solving a parametric family of problems, a task for which a general algorithm is proposed. The efficacy of this method is illustrated through examples involving image denoising and clustering. The proposed approach achieves satisfactory results for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian data. Chain Event Networks (CEMs) serve as a robust extension of Markov Logic Networks (MLNs), offering a practical framework for modeling complex systems through a blend of deterministic rules and probabilistic data. While Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) is a recognized technique for CEM selection that integrates model averaging with Bayesian model determination, it suffers from high computational costs and, more critically, relies on the often unrealistic assumption of parameter independence. This study introduces an alternative approach by adapting the Bayesian MAP (Best Match Approximation) framework from database query optimization. This method enables the independent and efficient selection of CEMs that align with both deterministic rules and probabilistic data. We demonstrate the method's efficacy using a case study of a large-scale CEM. Furthermore, the proposed framework is flexible enough to be extended for model averaging, a topic reserved for future research. The source code is accessible at https://github.com/ahmedhassan123/CEMSA. Our findings indicate that the Bayesian MAP framework is highly effective for large-scale CEMs, achieving a 1000-fold reduction in runtime compared to BMA. Additionally, the method is general and can be applied to other CEM tasks, such as learning and inference. The implementation is built upon the CEMLib library, which supports CEM modeling, learning, and inference. We have also developed a novel CEM model selection tool, available as a Python package named CEMSelect, with installation instructions provided at https://pypi.org/project/CEMSelect/. The CEMLib library can be installed via pip using the command `pip install CEMLib`. Finally, a CEM model was constructed from the UCI Heart Disease dataset to illustrate the application of this framework. The corresponding data, code, and model are available at https://github.com/ahmedhassan123/CEMSA/tree/master/data/heart_disease. The paper itself can be found at https://github.com/ahmedhassan123/CEMSA/tree/master/paper/CEMSA_paper.pdf. The source code is located at https://github.com/ahmedhassan123/CEMSA/tree/master/code/CEMSA_code.py. Additional code is accessible at https://github.com/ahmedhassan123/CEMSA/tree/master/code/CEMSA_code.ipynb. Finally, the CEM model is hosted at https://github.com/ahmedhassan

We introduce a robust asymptotic framework to analyze a specific inertial dynamics system, regulated by a vanishing Tikhonov regularization parameter $\gamma \to 0^+$, as it approaches the set of minimal norm solutions to a static equilibrium problem arising from convex optimization. Our robustness findings demonstrate that, regardless of the initial condition, the asymptotic behavior of the inertial method is reliably governed by the Euclidean distance to this minimal norm solution set. Specifically, we establish a nearly logarithmic convergence rate, mirroring that of the heavy ball algorithm, for both the objective function values and the iterates. Furthermore, we extend these robustness results to various accelerated proximal point methods designed for finding minimal norm solutions to variational inequalities involving $\alpha$-cocoercive operators. Finally, we rigorously validate the soundness of these asymptotic results by deriving a polynomial convergence rate towards a single saddle point of the Lagrangian associated with the Hamiltonian of the dynamical system. The effectiveness of our theoretical findings is confirmed through several numerical experiments. Notably, our approach offers a significant advantage over existing asymptotic analyses, which often rely on restrictive assumptions regarding initial conditions or the absence of regularization. Additionally, we provide a comprehensive review of the diverse applications of this inertial method. This paper examines the long-time asymptotic behavior of closed curves under the crystalline curvature flow, which shares characteristics with both the standard curvature flow and total variation flow. While the asymptotic dynamics for the standard curvature flow are well-established, the crystalline flow presents greater complexity due to the lack of comprehensive understanding of its long-time behavior. In the latter case, the asymptotic profile is characterized as a sequence of equilateral polygons whose side lengths may vary over time. This profile resembles the curvature flow but differs in allowing for nontrivial time-dependent limits, such as circles or their polygons, and can also result in non-compact limits. The total variation flow's crystal-like nature stems from the fact that its associated energy is the $L^1$ norm of the Laplacian of the curve, making its formal limit closely related to the curvature flow's limit but with the curvature term's sign reversed. This relationship highlights the distinct features of the crystalline flow's asymptotic dynamics, which are the primary focus of this survey. Additionally, we review recent findings by the first author and colleagues regarding crystalline curves with initial data close to equilateral polygons, demonstrating that their asymptotic behavior is more similar to the curvature flow than to the curvature flow with a sign change. Finally, we outline several open problems concerning the asymptotic behavior of the crystalline flow. This survey serves as a comprehensive overview of existing results and gaps regarding crystalline flow, with the aim of inspiring further research into its long-time asymptotic behavior. The study of this flow is motivated by its connection to the Mumford-Shah functional, a key component in Mumford and Oakley's seminal work on curve shortening and image segmentation. Furthermore, recent applications in curve fitting and image inpainting underscore the significance of understanding the asymptotic behavior of crystalline flows. The paper begins with an introduction to the Mumford-Shah functional and the Mumford-Oakley flow, followed by a presentation of the Mumford-Shah functional's variational approximations, including the crystalline flow and total variation flow. Finally, we provide an overview of the current state of the art concerning the well-posedness and long-time asymptotic behavior of these approximations. This background is essential for understanding the subsequent sections, which detail the asymptotic behavior of the crystalline flow. The paper concludes with a discussion of open problems related to the asymptotic behavior of the crystalline flow. Plants are vital to human survival, yet their form is dictated by environmental factors rather than human intent. This study introduces GrowSpace, a robotic system designed to cultivate plant sculptures by three-dimensionally modulating light intensity. The controller for GrowSpace employs a novel policy gradient reinforcement learning approach to automatically discover lighting conditions that foster healthy growth while shaping plants according to specific targets. We validated GrowSpace across two growth mediums—soil and air—demonstrating its ability to learn effective lighting policies and successfully sculpt plants in both environments. Furthermore, the system was deployed in a greenhouse over a three-week period to grow air plants capable of matching the height and width of the specified goals. These results confirm the feasibility of using reinforcement learning to automate the discovery of growth strategies for both soil and air plant cultivation. Our findings also highlight the potential of applying reinforcement learning to plant science to accelerate the understanding of growth mechanisms and to create engaging, user-defined botanical art. The GrowSpace code and experiments are available at https://github.com/PrincetonML/GrowSpace.

We establish a conformal gluing theorem for semi-infinite directed polymers on Liouang quantum disks and apply it to characterize the Schramm-Loewner-Knappaev (SLE$_{\kappa}$) process on the unit disk, where $\kappa \in [0, \infty)$. In this process, the trace generates a family of Liouang quantum disks, and probabilistic measures on these disks are derived by conformally gluing Liouang quantum disks corresponding to conditional measures on quantum wedges. Our proof relies on the polymer characterization of Liouang quantum wedges developed by the second author and O'Connell, the quantum Ito calculus for polymers, and recent findings regarding the quantum martingale. As a consequence, we derive an alternative characterization of the Liouang field necessary for constructing the disk partition function. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Liouang field can be uniquely determined from its disk partition function. This methodology extends to constructing conformally invariant measures on quantum hyperbolic surfaces. Additionally, we provide a sketch of how to construct an SLE$_{\kappa}$ process on the unit disk. Finally, we illustrate that our construction aligns with existing literature when $\kappa = 8/3$ and $\kappa = 4$. The image indicator initiative seeks to enhance the comparability of structural image quality metrics across different countries and institutions by establishing a unified framework for calculating structural indicators. This effort is grounded in extensive discussions regarding the interpretation of various imaging metrics and the standardization of protocols and methodologies. Although individual institutions may compute specific indicators using distinct protocols, there is a consensus that standard protocols should be adopted for specific indicators, and that the most prevalent protocols at a given institution are suitable for standardization. This document outlines the images and protocols necessary for standardizing selected structural indicators. While this initiative does not standardize the specific protocols or indicator values used internally at each institution, it aims to facilitate comparisons between different facilities. Furthermore, the initiative serves as a foundation for future developments in image quality standards. This image-based approach complements existing phantom-based initiatives, such as the QIBA IRM and the IETF XQI Image Analysis Task Group, which standardize physical performance metrics; together, these programs form a comprehensive framework for CT image quality. We anticipate that this report will stimulate further discussions aimed at standardizing structural image metrics. Additionally, we propose that a collaborative working group be established to advance the standardization of image indicators, building upon the groundwork laid in this report. This proposal will be shared with relevant organizations, including DICOM, IETF, and QIBA. Finally, we intend to make the images referenced in this report publicly available through an accessible platform, such as NiftyNet, to support research in image quality evaluation. We welcome any inquiries or contributions from the community. For further information, please contact CTImageQuality@siemens.com. This study investigates the $K\Lambda$ and $K\Sigma$ photoproduction reactions on a nucleon at rest using real photons. By applying the N/D method alongside a partial wave analysis, the resonance parameters for the $K\Lambda N$ and $K\Sigma N$ systems were determined. The analysis incorporated the $S_{1/2}$ and $P_{1/2}$ partial waves, which dominate the reaction in the energy range up to 1.2 GeV. To model the resonances, we utilized the functions $r_0$, $r_1$, and $r_2$ proposed by Gasser and Leutwyler. The $r_0$ and $r_1$ parameters exhibit weak energy dependence, whereas $r_2$ demonstrates a more pronounced sensitivity to energy variations. The calculated decay widths for the $S_{1/2}$ and $P_{1/2}$ resonances are presented in tables. Furthermore, future research should incorporate $\rho$-meson exchange mechanisms and extend the partial wave analysis to higher orders. Finally, the validity of these results requires verification through future experimental measurements. This study addresses vehicle platoon formation and regulation within a linked driving environment, specifically focusing on the dynamic joining of new vehicles to established platoons. The primary challenge lies in managing the impact of these joiners on the existing platoons, particularly when new vehicles attempt to insert themselves at optimal positions to maximize their own benefits, potentially disrupting the harmony of the pre-existing platoon. To address this, we introduce a dynamic contest model that facilitates the competition between incoming vehicles and relevant members of existing platoons. This mechanism aims to mitigate the negative effects of injections on the platoon while allowing individual participants to pursue their respective interests. We provide a detailed analysis of this model's properties and establish sufficient conditions guaranteeing system stability. Furthermore, numerical simulations are employed to demonstrate the model's effectiveness. The proposed framework offers a viable solution for regulating platoon behavior during vehicle joinings, presenting a valuable tool for the intelligent control of vehicle platoons. Additionally, the research findings may have broader applications in other automated driving systems. Finally, we outline several promising directions for future work. Notably, the mathematical model developed here is not restricted to vehicle platoon control and can be applied to various other fields. Specifically, the concepts of competition and harmony can be extended to numerous social systems, such as biological ecosystems, where they play a crucial role in maintaining system stability. The differential contests framework is also applicable to other areas, including the study of opinion dynamics and the control of multi-agent systems. Finally, the methodologies and findings presented can be utilized in the control of large-scale systems. It is a well-known phenomenon that including multiplicative interaction terms between two variables in a linear model often results in regions with opposing signs, causing the inclusion of such terms to feel counterintuitive. This paper demonstrates that within the local linear discriminant analysis framework, the decision rule for a logistic regression model incorporating an interaction term exhibits an effect similar to that of a concave function. Furthermore, it is proven that the decision region generated by a logistic regression model with an interaction term cannot be expressed as a finite union of rectangles. These findings are illustrated using data from the UCI Machine Learning Repository. Additionally, the study explores methods for selecting interaction terms, aiming to mitigate the identified drawbacks. The paper concludes with numerical examples comparing models with and without interaction terms. Finally, a Python library is introduced to facilitate the development of both types of models. All concepts presented are implemented in Python, and the material is designed to be accessible to readers with a basic understanding of programming. The discussion begins with fundamental statistical theory and progresses to an elementary introduction to the proposed library. The Python code for all examples is available at: https://github.com/ahmedhassan123/Logistic_Regression_With_Interaction. Headlines serve as concise summaries of news articles, typically written in a "inverted pyramid" structure where the most critical details appear first. This methodology is also prevalent in automatically generated summaries, which are often produced using extraction-based algorithms. These algorithms prioritize sentences containing the most significant information, a process frequently guided by human-curated guidelines. However, relying on expert input presents challenges regarding scalability and cost.

This study investigates the replacement of human experts with computational models to identify the most vital sentences in news articles. We introduce a novel dataset comprising 1.5 million news articles featuring pairs of original and automatically generated headlines. We train and assess transformer-based sequence classification models on this dataset to evaluate their capacity to predict headline sentences. Our findings indicate that these models can learn the underlying patterns of important sentence identification with high accuracy. Furthermore, we demonstrate that such models can assist journalists in efficiently pinpointing crucial sentences within news reports. Our results show that a simple transformer-based approach can achieve a precision of 80% in locating these significant sentences. Our code is accessible at https://github.com/abhishekgupta1999/recognizing-created-headlines.

Keywords: Automatic Summarization, Extractive Summarization, News Summarization, Important Sentence Recognition, Sequence Classification, Transformer Models.

We present a classical spin model that incorporates both Heisenberg and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, designed to capture the essential physics of the kagome lattice. By fine-tuning the coupling constants, we identify a kagome ice ground state featuring chiral frustration on the triangular sublattice. Monte Carlo simulations reveal that at finite temperatures, the system undergoes a continuous transition into a unique chiral spin fluid phase. This phase is characterized by a disordered spin configuration, rigid local chirals, and a spectral gap in the entropy spectrum. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this chiral spin fluid phase is accessible in a polycrystalline variant of our model, where the couplings are fixed at the values corresponding to the Heisenberg kagome antiferromagnet ground state. In this polycrystalline system, the chiral spin fluid phase emerges through a sequence of entropic and Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transitions. Finally, we discuss the experimental feasibility of observing this phase in classical spin ice materials. These findings suggest that engineering chiral spin fluid phases is feasible in spin ices by adjusting the exchange couplings. Additionally, our results indicate that the polycrystalline model, which is relevant to Heisenberg kagome antiferromagnets, also supports a low-temperature phase of chiral spin fluids. This represents a significant step toward realizing the kagome kagome phase, a quantum critical point between kagome ice and kagome liquid phases in the quantum spin ice model. Ultimately, our findings suggest that kagome ice and Heisenberg kagome antiferromagnets offer promising candidates for observing kagome ice and kagome liquid phases, respectively. Consequently, these systems could serve as a crucial testbed for investigating the quantum phase diagram of quantum kagome models. The core innovation involves applying a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to every baseline in the dataset. Additionally, we demonstrate that for regular-array observations, the gain matrix exhibits a block Toeplitz structure, enabling the calculation of the gain matrix inverse with $\mathcal{O}(N\log{N})$ computational cost and $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory usage. Consequently, the proposed method is highly efficient for both computation and memory requirements, making it suitable for the calibration of future-generation radio interferometers. Finally, we illustrate that this strategy is applicable to real data from the Low Frequency Array (LOFAR). Furthermore, we show that baselines with short projected baselines can be effectively utilized to correct gain variations across all frequencies and time intervals, thereby significantly enhancing the sensitivity of longer projected baselines. This study introduces a novel deep learning approach for portfolio allocation that utilizes Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to model the correlation structure of asset returns. We address a key limitation of GANs by integrating an attention mechanism to enhance performance on multivariate datasets. Furthermore, we propose employing conditional GANs to reduce the dimensionality of training data and improve training efficiency. Our results demonstrate that the network can accurately replicate the correlation structure of simulated data, even under scenarios where the underlying data distribution is non-Gaussian. Additionally, we evaluate the efficacy of this model in generating efficient frontiers for portfolio investment. Finally, we apply our framework to actual stock market data from the United States and Hong Kong. Given the relatively recent emergence of using GANs for portfolio allocation, there is currently a scarcity of literature on the topic; therefore, we aim to establish a foundation for future research in this area. Our work specifically addresses the underexplored challenges of non-Gaussian and high-dimensional data within the context of portfolio allocation. To our knowledge, this represents the first attempt to employ conditional GANs for portfolio allocation purposes. We anticipate that this approach will significantly advance future research in generative adversarial methods for investment allocation. The source code will be made publicly available to facilitate further scholarly investigation. This paper serves as a preliminary report. This study introduces a novel Bayesian framework utilizing a neural network to identify quasars within the third Fermi-LAT catalog of gamma-ray sources. The model incorporates an attention mechanism to highlight relevant features, such as source spectral indices, and is trained on a synthetically generated quasar sample. The resulting framework achieves a 70% quasar detection rate with a false-positive rate of 30%. Furthermore, the model's quasar classification performance remains robust across various gamma-ray source catalogs. The Bayesian approach leverages the uncertainty inherent in the training data to refine quasar identification. The Bayesian attention model demonstrates an R² score of 0.82, indicating that it captures the intrinsic relationships between source properties and the specific features that best distinguish quasars. This tool is expected to assist astronomers in the automated classification of gamma-ray point sources. The source code is accessible at https://github.com/abhishekkumar1998/Quasar-Classifier. Social media has become a primary channel for information dissemination and a key driver of online public relations. For individuals and organizations seeking to broaden their reach, it is essential to recognize the critical role of social media managers in managing accounts and generating content. However, for deaf and hard-of-hearing managers, creating accessible content remains a significant challenge. This study investigates the obstacles and potential strategies for content creation within social media management, drawing on data from an online survey of 100 hearing individuals and in-depth interviews with 10 hard-of-hearing participants. The findings reveal that all hearing respondents viewed social media management as a career, whereas only half of the hard-of-hearing respondents saw it as such. The remaining hard-of-hearing participants expressed a desire to pursue the role but faced barriers, including the perception that it is not a career, concerns about employment discrimination, and a lack of confidence in their abilities. Consequently, the report suggests that future content creation should prioritize accessibility by providing equal opportunities for deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals to engage in social media management. Additionally, organizations are encouraged to implement inclusive hiring practices and actively work to dismantle the notion that social media management excludes those with hearing impairments. This research holds particular relevance for organizations aiming to expand their influence and reach through social media platforms. Finally, the study underscores the necessity of further research into the specific challenges and solutions surrounding social media management for the deaf and hard-of-hearing community. The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is currently evaluating a mid-term space telescope mission, with the Indian Space and Astronomy Technology (INSIST) proposed as a candidate. Designed for both spectroscopic and imaging capabilities, this mission aims to investigate various scientific areas, including exoplanets, stellar populations, and the early universe. The primary instrument is a wide-field, multi-band optical camera featuring a 1.5-meter primary mirror, which will be deployed in a highly elliptical orbit around the Sun. This configuration ensures uninterrupted observations and minimizes stray light interference. The proposed orbit is anticipated to be provided by an indigenous Indian satellite platform, such as the Small Satellite Launching System (SSLV) or the Small Satellite Launching Platform (SSLP). The paper outlines the mission's scientific objectives, instrument specifications, and development roadmap, while also addressing key challenges and offering potential solutions. Additionally, the document references related projects, such as the AstroSat mission, to highlight relevant experiences. Ultimately, the study emphasizes the necessity of a dedicated, experienced development team to successfully execute the INSIST mission. Furthermore, the authors propose a comprehensive strategy for technology development, starting from the current stage and extending to the time of launch. Finally, the paper recommends a thorough feasibility study to provide a more robust roadmap for the project. The goal is to initiate development within the next 10 to 15 years, thereby enabling the realization of the INSIST mission. Keywords: Exoplanets, Stellar Populations, Early Universe, Wide-field Optical Camera, Space Telescope. (A longer version of this paper will be published as a book chapter by the author.)

We propose a likelihood ratio test for inferring change points in the second derivative of the spline and establish the asymptotic distribution of this test statistic. Furthermore, we develop a test for determining the optimal number of splines within the data. To address the challenge of AD being a chronic condition, we incorporate a random walk component into the spline model to represent the disease's progression. Additionally, we address the issue of data collection frequency declining over time. Our methods are validated using both Alzheimer's data and a Monte Carlo study. We introduce a global enhancement technique designed to magnify the cost associated with crossing low action regions, thereby facilitating a clearer identification of transition paths. By analyzing the resulting enhanced landscape, typical transformation trajectories can be readily observed. This approach functions as both a standalone method for discovering prevailing transition routes and as an preparatory step to refine the target pathway before applying stochastic dynamics. Its efficacy is validated across several representative examples, demonstrating its utility in revealing deterministic and stochastic transition paths, as well as in-noise stable and metastable transitions. Furthermore, the technique is applicable to any cost function derived from physical or non-physical systems. The findings are supported by video materials accessible at https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.14502088.1. Keywords: Transition path, Transition state, Action functional, Landscape analysis. Furthermore, this approach is applicable to a broad class of parabolic complex Hessian equations, specifically those of the form $H_{k}(\dot{D}u)=0$ where $k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. In these scenarios, the Hessian eigenvalues $\lambda(\dot{D}u)$ satisfy either $\lambda_{1}+\cdots+\lambda_{k}\geq 0$ or $\lambda_{1}\cdots\lambda_{k}\geq 0$. We establish the parabolic Hessian reverse curvature condition required to ensure the Hessian eigenvalues remain within the hinged cone. Additionally, the parabolic $H_{k}$-hinged condition is demonstrated to be sufficient for the existence of smooth solutions to the hinged equation. The study concludes with a discussion on the long-time behavior of these parabolic equations. Notably, for the equation $\det(D^{2}u)=0$ with $u\geq 0$, hinged boundary conditions naturally enforce the non-negativity of the Hessian eigenvalues. By applying the maximum principle, it is shown that the zero-order viscosity solution to the corresponding parabolic hinged equation is both unique and smooth. Finally, the paper presents a family of examples illustrating the necessity of the hinged condition. As an application, we examine the mean curvature flow of submanifolds under hinged boundary conditions, demonstrating that the flow preserves the hinged property. This result relies on the fact that the second fundamental form $\chi$ fulfills the hinged condition, and the evolution equation for $\chi$ is identified as a parabolic $H_{k}$-hinged equation. Furthermore, we prove that the hinged condition is maintained throughout the flow, provided the initial data is hinged and the solution exists. We present the direct and converse theorems regarding the convergence of the approximation sequence, alongside a uniqueness theorem for the equation under specific constraints. This study investigates the computational and logical characteristics of two subclasses of $n$-regular functions, which are defined by finite automata with a monoid of size $n$. We introduce a typed lambda calculus, derived from the simply typed lambda calculus, that precisely characterizes a broad spectrum of these functions across various types. In contrast to prior formalisms that struggled to express elementary properties of $n$-regular functions when $n \geq 3$, our calculus supports the definition of their characteristic functions and the formulation of their defining equations. This approach stems from an extended investigation into the expressivity of the term algebra of the calculus. Our research is grounded in an upper bound for the number of states required by a finite automaton to represent an $n$-regular function of a specific type. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this upper bound is tight for a significant class of vectorial $n$-regular functions. Finally, we outline several open questions and potential future research directions. These include extending the results to a wider class of $n$-regular functions, adapting the method to other subcategories of $n$-regular functions, and applying the findings to the theory of $n$-automatic sets. The proofs are supported by computer algebra systems, and we provide an appendix with code snippets written in a specialized language. This language is a variant of the calculus featuring an additional term that enumerates all ground terms of a given type, a term that can be eliminated from the calculus without affecting expressivity. The method for proving the main result relies on the computational capabilities provided by this enumeration term. We also discuss how to modify the proof when this technique is unavailable. The findings are presented as the first part of the author's thesis, which focuses on the algorithmic aspects of $n$-regular functions. The second part details the algorithm and its implementation. This text serves as a technical note examining the relationship between Itô and Stratonovich integrals when their integrands involve functions of conditional distributions within optimal filter flows. It highlights a specific characteristic of the Stratonovich integral with such integrands: it yields an explicit formula for the conditional distribution flow that aligns with the classical transformation rule for solutions to stochastic differential equations. Furthermore, a comparative analysis of both integral types is conducted through the lens of conditional distribution flows of Markov processes. Finally, the material finds application in monitoring and estimation tasks, where SDEs driven by nonlinear functionals of conditional distribution flows—arising from optimal filters—are utilized to derive performance metrics. In this context, the conditional flows of the marked processes associated with these SDEs are analyzed using Itô and Stratonovich integrals with appropriate specific functions. The study demonstrates that the Stratonovich integral offers a more convenient framework for solving the resulting SDEs and deriving performance indicator formulas. Additionally, the conditional distribution flow of the marked process of this SDE is derived via the Itô integral, with a verification of its consistency against the solution obtained through the Stratonovich integral approach. The notation, assumptions, and SDE selection are tailored to the authors' prior research and specific applications. However, the core findings remain valid under broader conditions, and the authors intend to explore these more general scenarios in future work. Keywords: Conditional distribution, optimal filter, Stratonovich integral, Itô integral, Markov process, Stochastic differential equation, performance indicator. This paper introduces a concept of quasi-characters extended to all groups and investigates their associated topology and maximal ideal space. For an abelian group $A$, the space of continuous quasi-characters under the topology of pointwise convergence coincides with the classical character space of $A$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the algebraic tensor product of quasi-character rings corresponds to the $C^\ast$-tensor product of the associated $A_\ast$-valued topological rings, provided the groups have cardinalities strictly less than $2^{\aleph_0}$. The tensor product of the standard structure spaces of such abelian groups is homeomorphic to the maximal structure space of the resulting $A_\ast$-valued topological ring. The paper also examines structure spaces for $p$-groups and free $p$-groups. Additionally, we define the spectral radius for $A$ and prove that it aligns with the classical spectral radius when $A$ is an abelian $k$-group for a field $k$ with cardinality greater than $|A|$. Finally, we outline several research questions arising from these findings. English translation by Mikhail Borovoi. Cross-domain text-to-SQL generation has garnered significant attention due to its practical utility in querying databases via natural language. However, existing approaches frequently produce suboptimal SQL statements, often resulting in syntactically incorrect outputs. To address this, this paper introduces a cross-domain methodology that integrates a symbolic parser to ensure syntactically correct SQL. Nevertheless, directly merging a symbolic parser with neural networks often degrades performance. Consequently, we propose treating the symbolic parser not as a component of the end-to-end network but as a separate, supportive task. Our results demonstrate that this approach enhances both the speed and accuracy of text-to-SQL generation compared to prior methods. Furthermore, the method yields state-of-the-art performance on the Spider benchmark. The code is accessible at https://github.com/1000000000000000000000000000000/SQL_Paper.git.

This study addresses secure navigation within multi-robot systems by introducing a risk-averse management method designed to mitigate collision risks during coordinated movements. This method employs a data-informed probabilistic collision model, utilizing real-time sensor data from robots and obstacles to generate an accurate collision probability model. The risk-averse management strategy subsequently minimizes this collision probability while ensuring robot navigation, security, and comfort. The efficacy of this approach is validated through simulation experiments, which demonstrate a significant reduction in collision probability and enhance the overall security of multi-robot systems. Additionally, the method's comfort is assessed using a multi-objective function that incorporates acceleration and control effort. Experimental results confirm that the proposed strategy achieves a superior balance between comfort and performance, as evidenced by the simulation outcomes. Finally, the method is applied to a real-world scenario involving a multi-legged robot navigating a complex environment, successfully demonstrating a trade-off between risk and comfort. The results indicate that the security of this multi-legged robot is improved through the use of the proposed method. The overall framework is implemented in MATLAB and made available as an open-source tool for risk-averse management in multi-robot systems. Keywords: Multi-Robot Systems, Risk-Averse Management, Collision Probability Model, Data-Informed Collision Probability Model, Model Predictive Control.

We introduce Andromeda XXV (And XXV), a unique dwarf galaxy characterized by a very low central dark matter density. This object was identified through the MUSE survey of the Andromeda galaxy group. Its discovery is notable for possessing a high metallicity of [Fe/H] = -0.12 ± 0.11, despite being located far from the Andromeda galaxy. We present the initial findings regarding And XXV, including its morphology, kinematics, and chemical composition. The galaxy exhibits a compact, bright core with a half-light radius of approximately 100 parsecs. The center displays a flat continuum spectrum, suggesting the presence of an old stellar population. Radial velocity data indicates that And XXV is on a highly eccentric orbit around Andromeda, with an eccentricity of 0.81. Furthermore, the galaxy is on its second or third pericentric passage, having been tidally stripped roughly 1.5 billion years ago. We propose that And XXV is a "leak" galaxy, having been captured by Andromeda during a past merger and subsequently stripped of its dark matter halo. This scenario is supported by the absence of dark matter within its central region. Additionally, we estimate the mass of And XXV to be approximately 1.5 billion solar masses. We conclude that And XXV is a valuable target for future research, as it offers a rare opportunity to study a dwarf galaxy in an early stage of interaction with a massive host like Andromeda. This study is the first in a series of four papers dedicated to the MUSE Andromeda survey. The remaining three papers will explore the properties of the remaining three galaxies identified in this work. Grant-free massive connectivity enables a vast number of devices to transmit data without allocating dedicated time or frequency resources, thereby conserving energy and expanding network capacity. This approach is particularly effective for applications involving frequent, small data transmissions from numerous low-power devices, such as those found in industrial control systems. This paper introduces a dual-stage genetic algorithm designed to generate a robust codebook of non-orthogonal patterns optimized for grant-free massive access. The initial stage focuses on creating a diverse set of non-orthogonal patterns, while the second stage selects an optimal codebook that maximizes both diversity and distinguishability. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance in error probability and system capacity compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques. Furthermore, the design process is shown to converge rapidly, typically requiring fewer than 100 generations. The method's efficacy is validated through extensive simulations using various metrics, including Hamming distance, Hamming weight, and inner product. Additionally, the proposed method is evaluated against multiple state-of-art solutions, such as Compressed Sensing, Random Binary Patterns, and Non-orthogonal Patterns, confirming its effectiveness. The results indicate that this method is especially suitable for grant-free massive connectivity in SC-QPSK modulation schemes. Finally, the method is highly general and can be adapted to other signaling schemes, like SC-PSK or FSK, by adjusting the objective function within the algorithm. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/ahmedhassan1990/Dual-Stage-Genetic-Algorithm}. The authors are currently working on extending the code to support other signaling schemes. This code is expected to be valuable for researchers in the field of grant-free massive connectivity. This study examines the M\o{}ller approximation and its thermodynamically consistent counterpart, the S\o{}rensen approximation, which are utilized for modeling humid air. The former is known for its computational efficiency, whereas the latter ensures greater thermodynamic accuracy. The molar internal energy is approximated by combining an ideal gas component with non-ideal contributions from individual species, augmented by a non-ideal interaction term specific to species pairs. We analyze how these approximations influence the predicted thermodynamic properties of the mixture. The research is supported by both theoretical analysis and numerical experiments. Our findings indicate that the S\o{}rensen approximation yields thermodynamic properties that align more closely with experimental data, while the M\o{}ller approximation introduces a more significant entropy error. Furthermore, we demonstrate that both approximations are equivalent to the virial approximation of order 2 when that equivalence is applied to an isothermal equation of state. Finally, the paper concludes that the S\o{}rensen approximation offers a more accurate alternative to the M\o{}ller approximation. The computational cost of the S\o{}rensen approximation is only marginally higher than that of the M\o{}ller approximation, making it a practical choice. Consequently, we contend that the S\o{}rensen approximation is preferable to the M\o{}ller approximation. All calculations were performed using the Python package Cantera. This paper introduces a new method for dialogue state monitoring (DSM) in dialogue systems. Our approach models the uncertainty of automatic speech recognition (ASR) and natural language understanding (NLU) within spoken dialogue using Word Confusion Networks (wCNs) and feature engineering, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this marks the first instance of modeling ASR uncertainty for the purpose of DSM. By aggregating individual wCNs from a sequence of utterances, we construct a joint ASR confusion network (jCN) that represents the cumulative uncertainty across that sequence. To extract AsrConfidence from the jCN, we propose a novel confidence metric based on path similarity, which identifies the most frequent words and phrases along the network's paths. Furthermore, we represent utterance-level NLU confidence as the confidence score of the final parse tree. We integrate these confidence metrics into a DSM framework that monitors state changes and resolves conflicts by leveraging the content of the confidence measure. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed DSM system effectively identifies and resolves conflicts in utterance sequences, outperforming a baseline DSM system that does not utilize utterance-level confidence. Additionally, we find that the confidence derived from path similarity outperforms state-of-the-art methods for identifying the most frequent word from a confusion network. Finally, we show that the proposed path similarity-based confidence metric is robust across varying levels of ASR model quality. To our knowledge, this is the first confidence metric applied to word confidence network compression. We demonstrate that the count of $\mu$-stable sheaves on a smooth genus $g$ curve, weighted by their ranks and twist sheaf classes, varies as a $C^0$ extension of a specific meromorphic function on the $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ character variety of the curve's fundamental group. This result generalizes the work of Brine and Lockhart concerning 2-dimensional Gopalan-Seshadri stable bundles on smooth $\mathbb{P}^2$. Furthermore, this count includes a weight of $(-1)^{\chi(E)}$ for an $E$ with rank and determinant corresponding to the input data, and for $g=0$, it precisely equals the number of $\mu$-stable sheaves, disregarding rank and determinant weights. Our approach relies on the connection between the character variety's geometry and the moduli space of $\mu$-stable sheaves, as established by Donaldson and Thomas, extended by Brine and Lockhart. By applying the Euler characteristic functor to a bicomplex derived from this extension, we derive the stated count. This method also enables the enumeration of $\mu$-stable sheaves on smooth $\mathbb{P}^2$ and $\mathbb{P}^1 \times \mathbb{P}^1$. Additionally, we establish the existence of the required $C^0$ extension for a more general context: $\mu$-stable vector bundles on surfaces with a fixed determinant. This broader formulation is necessary for our subsequent generalization to 3-dimensional varieties, which we outline in the paper's conclusion. Our results are valid for dimensions up to $n=3$. The primary technical hurdle in extending to $n=4$ involves the failure of the moduli space of $\mu$-stable vector bundles to be a smooth algebraic variety. This paper introduces a mathematical model for the minimal intricate structures within universal entry frameworks, which include mathematical, physical, and linguistic systems. The concept of "intricacy" is derived from the complexity of logical networks, specifically through the complexity of their nodes and the complexity of the connections between them. Nodes are characterized by the minimal number of bits required to represent their states, while the complexity of a connection refers to the minimum bits needed to define the relationship between two nodes. We demonstrate that structures achieving minimal intricacy in universal entry frameworks are remarkably simple, consisting of a single node with internal connections. The inherent complexity of these nodes is determined by the framework's alphabet size, a parameter that varies across different systems. Furthermore, the complexity of the connections between these nodes is governed by the relationships defined within the framework. Finally, we discuss the significance of intricacy as a measure for the minimum resources required to implement a universal machine for each framework. The results indicate that minimal intricacy corresponds to minimal resource consumption in mathematical machines, moderate consumption in physical machines, and substantial consumption in symbolic machines. Consequently, the concept of intricacy provides a quantitative basis for explaining the hierarchy among mathematical, physical, and symbolic machines. This approach offers a new perspective on the Hierarchy Problem in modern physics, suggesting that the hierarchy may arise from the fundamental differences in the intricacy of universal entry frameworks. Intricacy serves as a new physical quantity that can be applied to characterize the properties of matter and energy. Additionally, we propose that the minimal structures of universal entry frameworks represent a new state of matter, which we term "universal matter." We outline the properties of this matter and suggest that it may be a viable candidate for dark matter. Finally, we conclude that the intricate nature of universal matter provides a potential solution to the problem of matter-antimatter asymmetry. A detailed analysis of these results will be presented in a future publication. By utilizing symbolic representations, this framework offers a new approach to understanding the properties of matter and energy. The universal entry framework is a universal symbolic representation that describes the relationship between the intricate structures of universal matter and the universal machine. This paper will provide a detailed analysis of the properties of universal matter, with a focus on the concept of intricacy and its application to the Hierarchy Problem and matter-antimatter asymmetry. We introduce a general framework for optimally verifying entanglement in multi-qubit optical quantum systems. This approach is grounded in the universal structure of entanglement witnesses, which are derived from optimal quantum state tomography. Unlike existing methods that rely on unknown unitary transformations or maximal measurement visibility, our scheme enables the unambiguous identification of whether a set of measurements constitutes a valid entanglement witness. We demonstrate that a complete set of such witnesses can be algorithmically generated for arbitrary optical quantum systems. Furthermore, we present examples of these witnesses for optical GHZ states and compare our proposed method with techniques based on random access codes. This work establishes a foundation for the comprehensive analysis of optical quantum systems. This study presents a novel perspective on the nature of JET tokamak perturbations, grounded in a new hypothesis. We contend that these disturbances are not intrinsic to the tokamak's operation but are instead induced by the Poincaré sections created at the rational surfaces where magnetic field lines intersect the poloidal limiter. This proposed mechanism offers an alternative explanation for various observed phenomena, including the origin of island widths, the formation of neoclassical heat transport, and the emergence of "Palm Tree Modes." Specifically, the observed "Palm Tree Modes" are explained as a resonant amplification of entropy generated by these Poincaré sections, which is driven by the Inter-Elipsoidal Instability (EI). This resonant amplification occurs at the rational q-values where the Poincaré sections are located. Furthermore, the stability characteristics of these perturbations on the low-q inner plasma edge closely mirror the general stability properties of standard single-peaked resonances found on rational islands. Finally, we suggest that the term "Palm Tree Modes" is misleading and should be replaced with "Poincaré-Tree Modes" to more accurately reflect their true origin. A detailed explanation of this naming convention can be found in our previous work, available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.07750. This manuscript serves as a translation of that original paper into English. Additionally, we provide a new, more comprehensive explanation for the observation of Palm Tree Modes on the Poincaré sections of JET limitors, which was previously proposed in Ref. [1]. Finally, we outline the general stability characteristics of these modes, which are governed by the EI stability properties on rational values of q. These conclusions are supported by detailed numerical calculations. Given that the EI mechanism is well-documented in the literature, the identification of Palm Tree Modes as a manifestation of EI provides a new insight into plasma physics. To facilitate this, we have translated the paper from Ref. [1] into English and included all supporting numerical calculations. We believe this work will be of significant interest to the plasma physics community.

This study addresses the task of identifying hate speech across three social media platforms—Facebook, Twitter, and Reddit—using multiple modalities: text, images, and user profiles. To enhance model interpretability and enable more effective countermeasures against hate speech, we incorporate three explanation techniques into our framework. Furthermore, we introduce a novel dataset of user-generated comments annotated with self-reported reasons for posting, allowing us to assess whether our classifications align with users' own motivations. Finally, we analyze the strengths and limitations of integrating these reason-based annotations into classification systems. These findings offer new avenues for leveraging reason-based information in hate speech classification and suggest promising future research directions for natural language processing. This study examines how axonal growth variability influences the development of neural networks. By employing a statistical analysis of randomly generated networks of type-I neurons, we demonstrate that the distribution of synaptic extents significantly alters the distribution of neural field coupling strengths. Furthermore, we show that the distribution of coupling strengths impacts the dynamics of the field's activity levels. Specifically, networks featuring long-range connections exhibit either no solutions or only unstable ones, whereas short-range connections produce stable solutions. These findings offer a qualitative explanation for the mechanisms driving axonal growth and their consequences on network structure and dynamics. Additionally, our results align with neurobiological evidence indicating that axonal growth is driven by molecular gradients and relies on the availability of receptors. Finally, we provide an interpretation of the observed phenomena using percolation theory. This work is part of a broader research initiative exploring the statistical properties of random networks, their dynamic behavior, and their application to understanding the human brain. Program repair systems generate syntactically correct fixes for specific bugs, categorized into effective fixes that resolve issues and non-effectiveness fixes that fail. To improve machine learning repair models, it is essential to distinguish these two types. This paper introduces Antagonistic Patch Creation (APC), a technique designed to synthesize program patches where the input program remains unmodified by the patch. We apply APC to create a new dataset for self-debugging languages, called the synthetic debug dataset (SDD), which includes programs paired with patches. In SDD, patches are antagonistic: they are correct relative to one another but incorrect relative to the input programs. Experimental results demonstrate that incorporating SDD into existing programs and patches enhances the performance of the PaSS model on conventional buggy programs. Additionally, we illustrate how the SDD dataset can be utilized to evaluate automated program repair systems across various languages. The capability region (CR) of a graph is defined as the union of the spectra of all its subgraphs. This concept was recently explored in the paper "On the capability region of a path graph" within Linear Algebra and its Applications, which demonstrated that the CR of a path graph $P_n$ forms a line segment connecting the spectra of $P_1$ (a single vertex) and $P_2$ (two connected vertices). This article generalizes those findings in two significant ways. First, we examine graphs with non-negative entries, proving that their capability region is convex—a property not necessarily true for general graphs. This finding enables the construction of a novel family of matrices, denoted $A_{k,n}$, whose capability region is precisely the line segment connecting the spectra of $A_{k,1}$ and $A_{k,2}$. Second, we investigate the continuous capability region (CCR), defined as the set of spectra for all possible continuous deformations of a graph. We establish that the CCR of $A_{k,n}$ is the entire complex plane, a stark contrast to the bounded, one-dimensional CR. Furthermore, we provide a characterization of matrices with a CCR equal to the entire complex plane and demonstrate that the CCR of a matrix is invariant under matrix similarity. The study begins with the definition and fundamental properties of the CR and CCR, followed by an outline of the paper's structure. Section 2 addresses the convexity of the CR for graphs featuring non-negative entries. In Section 3, we define the CCR and present methods for calculating it, starting with grid graphs. The final section introduces the concept of the continuous deformed spectrum, which is essential for understanding the CCR. Finally, in Section 4, we analyze the specific case of graph capability regions by linking the eigenvalues of a graph matrix to the roots of a corresponding polynomial. This approach yields the exact capability region for a specific class of matrices and, more broadly, allows for the calculation of the CR for matrices where the degree of the characteristic polynomial does not exceed 2. The capability region of a matrix is defined by the union of the spectra of all its submatrices, and the techniques developed in this work are applicable to the study of such regions. Keywords: Capability Region, Continuously Deformed Spectrum, Eigenvalues, Eigenvalues Regions, Graph Spectrum, Matrix Spectrum. Mathematics Subject Classification: 05C50, 15A18, 15A15,

The collision course and resulting characteristics of matter generated in heavy-ion collisions are now being explored through the lens of flow dynamics. This study introduces a new tool designed to analyze flow data, investigate the collision processes involved, and determine the equation of state for nuclear matter. Utilizing a newly developed theoretical framework, the 3-dimensional flow examination decomposes experimentally measured flow coefficients into three distinct components: the initial spatial anisotropy, the anisotropy generated during the collision evolution, and an asymmetrical flow arising from the asymmetrical initial conditions of the colliding nuclei. The 3D component linked to the initial anisotropy offers significant insights into the spatial structure of the initial collision configuration, whereas the flow generated during evolution is essential for examining the equation of state. The novel 3D examination demonstrates substantial potential for advancing our understanding of the collision process. Furthermore, the newly introduced asymmetrical flow component is expected to offer critical insights into the initial collision setup, which has previously been overlooked. The validity of this 3D approach was assessed using both idealized initial conditions and realistic scenarios derived from the Monte Carlo Glauber model, alongside realistic final flow coefficients calculated with the iEBE-VISHNU model. The results indicate that this 3D examination holds great promise for enhancing our knowledge of the collision process. Detecting COVID-19 early is crucial for mitigating its severe health impacts. While medical imaging is a common method for diagnosis, it often requires patients to visit hospitals or clinics, thereby increasing the risk of viral transmission. Consequently, utilizing non-invasive data like speech for early detection is a more preferable alternative. However, the presence of COVID-19 in speech data is not definitive; it merely indicates a higher likelihood of infection. This uncertainty complicates the task, as models trained on such data must be capable of concluding that a patient does not have COVID-19. This paper introduces a novel approach to both detect and rule out COVID-19 in speech through adversarial training, ensuring that model predictions remain independent of the presence of COVID-19. Experimental results using the V-CT19 dataset demonstrate the model's effectiveness, with the speech-based system achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.95 for detection and 0.93 for ruling out the disease. Furthermore, the study confirms the model's robustness against various attacks, including data poisoning, adversarial, and membership inference attacks. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have recently become a leading approach for analyzing complex graph-based systems, including wireless networks. However, current GNN architectures typically depend on centralized training and inference, which restricts their applicability in safety-critical wireless environments. This paper introduces \textit{GNN$^{DC}$}, a wireless transmission architecture designed to support a general class of GNNs while maintaining decentralized control. We validate the efficacy of \textit{GNN$^{DC}$} through an AN/PRC-66 radio case study, demonstrating that it achieves performance nearly identical to a centralized baseline under near-perfect conditions, with an average overhead of just 1.14%. Furthermore, our analysis of security and fault tolerance reveals that \textit{GNN$^{DC}$} incurs only a marginal 0.11% drop in performance when subjected to various security threats and fault injection scenarios. These findings indicate that \textit{GNN$^{DC}$} enables wireless transmission systems to integrate intelligent, graph-based applications in a decentralized fashion, thereby enhancing their safety and security resilience. This work introduces a new acceleration technique designed to transform stochastic gradient ascent with noise into stochastic gradient descent (or ascent) featuring challenge-adaptive updates. The resulting method, stochastic gradient descent with challenge-adaptive updates (SGD-CAT), converges at optimal rates under broad conditions, including those where standard accelerated ascent fails to converge. Furthermore, SGD-CAT exhibits robustness to various types of noise, making it applicable to scenarios where standard accelerated ascent does not converge. In practical applications, this approach can significantly accelerate inference and learning, particularly when dealing with data distributions characterized by high challenges or noise levels. Additionally, we apply SGD-CAT to training Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and demonstrate superior performance compared to standard accelerated methods. Our empirical findings indicate that SGD-CAT achieves faster training speeds, superior generator performance, and more stable training dynamics across a wide range of GAN configurations. Finally, we present evidence that SGD-CAT can train models from pre-trained checkpoints, a capability that other accelerated methods lack. This paper introduces a new category of self-exciting systems, characterized by a count process $N(t)$ and a set of $n$-dimensional marks $X(t)$. Unlike traditional self-exciting models, which rely on scalar state variables, these systems possess an infinite-dimensional state space defined by the trajectory of $N(t)$ and the history of $X(t)$. The dynamics are governed by a state equation that captures the evolution of $N(t)$ and a jump equation for $X(t)$, with jumps occurring at the times of $N(t)$. The proposed framework encompasses both classical self-exciting systems and coupled event flow systems as special cases. Furthermore, the study provides a novel representation of Poisson processes and marks processes within this general framework, establishing their corresponding random measure representations. A key feature of this general framework is its ability to model the correlation between the increments of the counting process and the marks; such correlation is absent in classical self-exciting systems. The paper concludes with a specific example that falls outside the class of classical self-exciting systems. Additionally, utilizing this general framework, the authors develop a new type of multi-type branching process, deriving its associated Feller equation. This Feller equation exhibits a structure analogous to that of classical branching processes but operates on an infinite-dimensional state space. Finally, the work derives the marginal distribution of the velocity process for this novel multi-type branching process, revealing a connection to Poisson processes. This study represents the initial step toward developing a theory for this new class of self-exciting systems. To facilitate this, the authors also extend several fundamental concepts from classical self-exciting system theory to the general framework, including the intensity function, the superposition and sub-addition properties, and the Poisson case. These extensions are executed via point process representations, specifically the time set and jump measure formulations. The resulting theory for this generalization is expected to be applicable to various other generalizations of self-exciting systems. Notably, this research also contributes to the theory of coupled event flow systems. Specifically, the paper demonstrates that the superposition of two coupled event flow systems remains a coupled event flow system, and it develops the theory of Poisson coupled event flow systems. These developments are achieved through the application of point process representations. Additionally, the paper presents a theory for multi-type branching processes based on the proposed generalization of single-type branching processes.
